```{r setup}
library("tidyverse")
library("sf")
library("rnaturalearth")
library("lme4")
library("lmerTest")
library("broom")
library("broom.mixed")
```

```{r import}

sugarbeet.phenology_dat <- read_delim("https://opendata.dwd.de/climate_environment/CDC/observations_germany/phenology/annual_reporters/crops/historical/PH_Jahresmelder_Landwirtschaft_Kulturpflanze_Zucker-Ruebe_1925_2024_hist.txt", trim_ws = TRUE)

code_list <- read_csv2("https://opendata.dwd.de/climate_environment/CDC/help/PH_Beschreibung_Phase.txt", locale = locale(encoding = "latin1"))

location_list <- read_delim("https://opendata.dwd.de/climate_environment/CDC/observations_germany/phenology/annual_reporters/farming/historical/PH_Beschreibung_Phaenologie_Stationen_Jahresmelder.txt", locale = locale(encoding = "latin1", decimal_mark = ".", grouping_mark = ","), delim = ";")

germany_sf <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf", country = "Germany", type = "map_units")
bundeslaender_sf <- ne_states(country = "Germany", returnclass = "sf")

```

```{r tidy}

bundeslaender_sf <- bundeslaender_sf |> 
  dplyr::select("regional_state" = name) |> 
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

code_list <- code_list |> 
  dplyr::select("Phase_id" = Phase_ID, Phase_englisch)

location_list <- location_list |> 
  dplyr::select(Stations_id, geograph.Breite, geograph.Laenge) |> 
  mutate(Stations_id = as.double(Stations_id),
         geograph.Breite = as.double(geograph.Breite),
         geograph.Laenge = as.double(geograph.Laenge))

sugarbeet.phenology_dat <- sugarbeet.phenology_dat |> 
  left_join(code_list) |> 
  filter(Phase_englisch == "beginning of tilling sowing drilling") |> 
  dplyr::select(Stations_id, Referenzjahr, Eintrittsdatum) |> 
  mutate(Eintrittsdatum = ymd(Eintrittsdatum)) |> 
  left_join(location_list) |> 
  drop_na() |> 
  group_by(Stations_id) |> 
    mutate("Messjahre" = n()) |> 
  ungroup()

sugarbeet.phenology_sf <- st_as_sf(sugarbeet.phenology_dat, coords = c("geograph.Laenge", "geograph.Breite"), crs = 4326)  

# Aggregation of small regional states to get a robust spatial scale
sugarbeet.phenology_sf <- sugarbeet.phenology_sf |> 
  st_join(bundeslaender_sf) |> 
  mutate(regional_state = case_when(regional_state %in% c("Schleswig-Holstein", "Hamburg") ~ "Schleswig-Holstein und Hamburg",
                                    regional_state %in% c("Niedersachsen", "Bremen") ~ "Niedersachsen und Bremen",
                                    regional_state %in% c("Brandenburg", "Berlin") ~ "Brandenburg und Berlin",
                                    regional_state %in% c("Rheinland-Pfalz", "Saarland") ~ "Rheinland-Pfalz und Saarland",
                                    TRUE ~ regional_state))

```

```{r SowingDate_Data, fig.asp=1}

illu_points <- sugarbeet.phenology_sf  |> 
  st_transform(crs = 25832) |> 
  mutate(recent = ifelse(Referenzjahr == 2023, "Yes", "No"))

plot_ <- ggplot(illu_points) + 
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(text = element_text(family = "Helvetica Neue"),
        legend.background = element_blank(),
        legend.position = c(0, 1),
        legend.justification = c(0, 1),
        legend.spacing.y = unit(0, "lines")) +
  geom_sf(data = germany_sf) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = Referenzjahr, size = recent), shape = 21, stroke = 0.1) +

  labs(fill = "Observation year",
       size = "Recent observation (2023)",

                             Phenological observations of crops from sowing to harvest
                             (annual reporters, historical), Version v010, 2024.
                             
    Till Rose",
       title = "Seven decades of sowing date observations\nin sugar beet") + 
  coord_sf(
    xlim = st_bbox(illu_points)[c("xmin", "xmax")] + c(-140000, 10000),
    ylim = st_bbox(illu_points)[c("ymin", "ymax")] + c(-65000, 90000),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
```

```{r SowingDate_Trend, fig.width = 5, fig.height=7}

illu <- sugarbeet.phenology_sf |> 
  sf::`st_geometry<-`(NULL) |> 
  mutate(doy = lubridate::yday(Eintrittsdatum)) |> 
  filter(doy > 30,
         doy < 155,
         Referenzjahr > 1950,
         Referenzjahr <= 2025) |> 
  mutate(Stations_id = factor(Stations_id)) |> 
  drop_na(regional_state) |> 
  # Centered year: with only 12 regions, letting regional_state have a
  # random slope on raw Referenzjahr (~1950-2025) makes the region-level
  # intercept variance numerically unstable (it's extrapolated to year 0).
  # Centering fixes this. It's also used *inside* the spline (instead of
  # raw Referenzjahr) so bs() and the random slope refer to literally the
  # same variable -- using two different transforms of "year" in the same
  # formula previously confused ggpredict()'s handling of the interaction.
  mutate(year_c = Referenzjahr - 1987)

model_lmm <- lmer(
  doy ~ splines::bs(year_c, df = 5) + (1 + year_c | regional_state) + (1 | Stations_id),
  data = illu,
  REML = TRUE,
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

summary(model_lmm)

# Fixed-effect (population-level, shared shape) trend with confidence interval
fixed_trend <- tidy(model_lmm, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE)
fixed_trend

# Overall (population-level) predicted trend: just the fixed spline shape,
# with every random effect (region and station) held out via re.form = NA
# -- i.e. no regional_state grouping, unlike the BLUPs used further down in
# SowingDate_Trend_Diagnostics.
pred_trend <- data.frame(
  year_c = seq(min(illu$year_c), max(illu$year_c), by = 1)
)
pred_trend$predicted <- predict(model_lmm, newdata = pred_trend, re.form = NA)
pred_trend$Referenzjahr <- pred_trend$year_c + 1987

plot_ <- ggplot() +
  theme_bw(base_size = 15) +
  theme(text = element_text(family = "Helvetica Neue"),
        legend.background = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        panel.grid = element_blank()) +
  geom_point(data = illu, aes(x = Referenzjahr, y = doy), alpha = 0.06, stroke = 0.2, shape = 21, fill = "grey") +
  geom_line(
    data = pred_trend,
    aes(x = Referenzjahr, y = predicted),
    colour = "blue",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year", y = "Sowing date (day of year)",
    title = "Overall sowing date trend",
    caption = "Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD), Climate Data Center (CDC):
                             Phenological observations of crops from sowing to harvest
                             (annual reporters, historical), Version v010, 2024.
                             
    Till Rose"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(add = c(1, 1))) +
  NULL

plot_


```

```{r SowingDate_Germany_RandomIntercept_and_StateEffect}


year_c_2023 <- 2023 - 1987

region_ranef_2023 <- ranef(model_lmm)$regional_state |> 
  tibble::rownames_to_column("regional_state") |> 
  dplyr::rename(region_intercept = `(Intercept)`, region_slope = year_c) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(region_effect_2023 = region_intercept + region_slope * year_c_2023) |> 
  dplyr::select(regional_state, region_effect_2023)

# Stations_id -> regional_state lookup, needed to attach each station's
# region effect alongside its own station-level intercept.
station_region <- illu |> 
  dplyr::distinct(Stations_id, regional_state) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(Stations_id = as.character(Stations_id))

station_ranef_map <- ranef(model_lmm)$Stations_id |> 
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Stations_id") |> 
  dplyr::rename(station_intercept = `(Intercept)`) |> 
  dplyr::left_join(station_region, by = "Stations_id") |> 
  dplyr::left_join(region_ranef_2023, by = "regional_state") |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    Stations_id = as.double(Stations_id),
    combined_effect_2023 = station_intercept + region_effect_2023
  )

# One point per station: sugarbeet.phenology_sf has one row per
# station-year, so take the distinct station/geometry combination and join
# on the combined station + region effect.
station_points_sf <- sugarbeet.phenology_sf |> 
  dplyr::distinct(Stations_id, geometry) |> 
  sf::st_as_sf() |> 
  dplyr::inner_join(station_ranef_map, by = "Stations_id")

plot_germany_ranef <- ggplot() +
  theme_minimal() +
  geom_sf(data = germany_sf, fill = "white") +
  geom_sf(data = bundeslaender_sf, fill = NA, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = station_points_sf, aes(colour = combined_effect_2023), size = 1, alpha = 1,) +
  scale_colour_gradient2(low = "#B2182B", mid = "white", high = "#2166AC", midpoint = 0) +
  labs(
    colour = "Station + region\neffect in 2023 (days)",
    title = "Combined station + regional deviation from the population-level trend (2023)"
  ) +
  NULL

plot_germany_ranef

```

```{r SowingDate_Germany_Interpolated}


station_points_m <- sf::st_transform(station_points_sf, 25832)
germany_sf_m <- sf::st_transform(germany_sf, 25832)
bundeslaender_sf_m <- sf::st_transform(bundeslaender_sf, 25832)

station_df <- station_points_m |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  dplyr::bind_cols(as.data.frame(sf::st_coordinates(station_points_m)))

gam_fit <- mgcv::gam(combined_effect_2023 ~ s(X, Y, k = 150), data = station_df, method = "REML")

# Prediction grid: 1km centres (bumped up from 5km for a visibly smoother
# raster/render), restricted to points that actually fall inside Germany's
# outline (so nothing is interpolated offshore or across the border).
grid_sf <- sf::st_make_grid(germany_sf_m, cellsize = 1000, what = "centers") |>
  sf::st_as_sf() |>
  sf::st_filter(germany_sf_m)

grid_interp_df <- as.data.frame(sf::st_coordinates(grid_sf))
grid_interp_df$combined_effect_2023 <- predict(gam_fit, newdata = grid_interp_df)

# Unlike IDW, a GAM smoother extrapolates everywhere by default, so
# distance-to-nearest-station has to be masked out manually: grid cells
# more than 15km from any reporting station (e.g. the North Frisian
# islands, or sparse stretches near the Bodensee/borders) get dropped
# rather than showing an extrapolated value, so those areas stay blank
# on the map instead of showing made-up values.
nearest_station_idx <- sf::st_nearest_feature(grid_sf, station_points_m)
grid_interp_df$dist_to_station <- as.numeric(
  sf::st_distance(grid_sf, station_points_m[nearest_station_idx, ], by_element = TRUE)
)

# grid_interp_df <- grid_interp_df |> dplyr::filter(dist_to_station <= 10000)

# True elevation contours (not contours of the fitted effect itself) let
# us check whether the "earlier sowing" ridges visually line up with real
# valleys (Rhine/Main/Danube) and uplands (e.g. the Harz), rather than just
# tracing the smoothed surface's own isolines. `geodata::elevation_30s()`
# pulls ~1km-resolution SRTM elevation for the country; reproject/crop/mask
# it to the same metric CRS and outline used for the effect surface.
elev <- geodata::elevation_30s(country = "DEU", path = tempdir())
elev_m <- elev |>
  terra::project("EPSG:25832") |>
  terra::crop(terra::vect(germany_sf_m)) |>
  terra::mask(terra::vect(germany_sf_m))

elev_df <- as.data.frame(elev_m, xy = TRUE)
names(elev_df) <- c("X", "Y", "elevation")

plot_germany_ranef_interp <- ggplot() +
  theme_minimal() +
  geom_sf(data = germany_sf_m, fill = "grey") +
  geom_tile(data = grid_interp_df, aes(x = X, y = Y, fill = combined_effect_2023)) +
  geom_contour(
    data = elev_df,
    aes(x = X, y = Y, z = elevation),
    colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.15, alpha = 0.5, binwidth = 250
  ) +
  geom_sf(data = bundeslaender_sf_m, fill = NA, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#B2182B", mid = "white", high = "#2166AC", midpoint = 0) +
  labs(
    fill = "Station + region\neffect in 2023 (days)",
    title = "Smoothed sowing-date effect with true elevation contours (200m)",
    x = "",
    y = ""
  ) +
  NULL

plot_germany_ranef_interp

```

```{r SowingDate_Germany_Interpolated_Rayshader}


bbox_m <- sf::st_bbox(germany_sf_m)
bbox_m[c("xmin", "ymin")] <- bbox_m[c("xmin", "ymin")] - 50000
bbox_m[c("xmax", "ymax")] <- bbox_m[c("xmax", "ymax")] + 50000


grid_full_sf <- sf::st_make_grid(sf::st_as_sfc(bbox_m), cellsize = 1000, what = "centers") |>
  sf::st_as_sf()
grid_full_df <- as.data.frame(sf::st_coordinates(grid_full_sf))

# legend.position = "none" is baked directly into gg_color itself here
# (matching gg_height below), rather than relying on a "+ theme(...)"
# tacked on wherever gg_color gets passed to plot_gg(). gg_color_legend,
# defined further down right before the standalone cowplot legend, is the
# one place that adds the legend back.
gg_color <- ggplot() +
  geom_tile(data = grid_full_df, aes(x = X, y = Y), fill = "grey50") +
  geom_tile(data = grid_interp_df, aes(x = X, y = Y, fill = combined_effect_2023)) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#B2182B", mid = "white", high = "#2166AC", midpoint = 0) +
  coord_equal(xlim = bbox_m[c("xmin", "xmax")], ylim = bbox_m[c("ymin", "ymax")], expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(fill = "Deviation from the national mean (days)")


neighbour_countries <- c("DEU", "NLD", "BEL", "LUX", "FRA", "CHE", "AUT", "CZE", "POL", "DNK")
elev_tiles <- lapply(neighbour_countries, function(cc) {
  geodata::elevation_30s(country = cc, path = tempdir(), mask = FALSE)
})
elev_mosaic <- do.call(terra::merge, elev_tiles)

elev_bbox_m <- elev_mosaic |>
  terra::project("EPSG:25832") |>
  terra::crop(terra::ext(bbox_m[c("xmin", "xmax", "ymin", "ymax")]))


# The only NAs left at this point are real gaps in the SRTM tiles -- just
# the North Sea/Baltic coastline in the north of the bbox, where sea level
# (0m) is a reasonable fill rather than an arbitrary one.
elev_bbox_m[is.na(elev_bbox_m)] <- 0

elev_bbox_df <- as.data.frame(elev_bbox_m, xy = TRUE)
names(elev_bbox_df) <- c("X", "Y", "elevation")

# Height ggplot: fill colour itself doesn't matter (plot_gg re-derives a
# greyscale height map from the underlying data values/scale), but a
# scale needs to be present so plot_gg can detect which aesthetic to use.
gg_height <- ggplot(elev_bbox_df, aes(x = X, y = Y, fill = elevation)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "black", high = "white") +
  coord_equal(xlim = bbox_m[c("xmin", "xmax")], ylim = bbox_m[c("ymin", "ymax")], expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")


rayshader::plot_gg(shadow_intensity = 0.6,
  gg_color,
  ggobj_height = gg_height,
  width = 5, height = 6.5,
  scale = 200,
  multicore = TRUE,
  windowsize = c(800, 1000),
  zoom = 0.55, phi = 90, theta = 0,
  raytrace = TRUE, sunangle = 260
)

# render_snapshot() has no "return the image, don't display it" mode --
# passing a filename just saves a PNG instead of plotting to a device, so
# that's used to get the render into an R object: save to a temp PNG, then
# read it back in with png::readPNG() as a plain height x width x RGB
# array, which annotation_raster() below can drop straight into a ggplot.
snapshot_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
rayshader::render_snapshot(filename = snapshot_path)
rgl::close3d()
snapshot_img <- png::readPNG(snapshot_path)

# coord_fixed(expand = FALSE) with xlim/ylim set to the image's own pixel
# dimensions keeps annotation_raster() filling the whole panel edge to
# edge (in image pixel units) rather than leaving ggplot's usual default
# expansion/margins around it.
gg_snapshot <- ggplot() +
  annotation_raster(snapshot_img, xmin = 0, xmax = ncol(snapshot_img), ymin = 0, ymax = nrow(snapshot_img)) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(0 + 36, ncol(snapshot_img) - 36), ylim = c(0 + 10, nrow(snapshot_img) - 10), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10))

# Legend as a patchwork inset, since gg_color itself has legend.position =
# "none" (needed so plot_gg() doesn't bake a colour bar into the terrain
# texture) and so isn't shown in the 3D render above. gg_color_legend on
# its own is still the *whole map* with a legend attached (just not
# suppressed) -- inset_element() would draw that entire small map on top
# of the big one. What's actually wanted is just the legend key itself:
# cowplot::get_legend() pulls that one grob out, and cowplot::ggdraw()
# wraps it back into a plain ggplot so inset_element() has something it
# can position. A translucent white background box behind it keeps the
# numbers legible against the terrain underneath. inset_element()'s
# left/bottom/right/top are fractions (0-1) of gg_snapshot's panel, so
# this sits in the upper-right corner.
gg_color_legend <- gg_color +
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "Helvetica Neue"),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(colour = "white", size = 12),
    legend.title = element_text(colour = "white", size = 12, vjust = 2.8),
    legend.key.spacing.y = margin(t = 1, unit = "lines"),
    legend.margin = margin(6, 8, 6, 8)
  )
gg_legend_only <- cowplot::ggdraw(cowplot::get_legend(gg_color_legend))

plot_ <- gg_snapshot +
  patchwork::inset_element(gg_legend_only, left = -0.12, bottom = 0.62, right = 0.98, top = 1.08) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(title = "Spatial variation in sugar beet sowing date",
                             caption = "Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD), Climate Data Center (CDC):
                             Phenological observations of crops from sowing to harvest
                             (annual reporters, historical), Version v010, 2024.
                             
    Till Rose") &
  theme(title = element_text(colour = "black", size = 13, vjust = 6, family = "Helvetica Neue"),
        caption = element_text(colour = "black", size = 10, vjust = 6, family = "Helvetica Neue"))


plot_

```

```{r SowingDateEarlier_RegionalState, fig.asp = 1}

state_to_region <- tibble::tribble(
  ~state,                          ~regional_state,
  "Schleswig-Holstein",            "Schleswig-Holstein und Hamburg",
  "Hamburg",                       "Schleswig-Holstein und Hamburg",
  "Niedersachsen",                 "Niedersachsen und Bremen",
  "Bremen",                        "Niedersachsen und Bremen",
  "Nordrhein-Westfalen",           "Nordrhein-Westfalen",
  "Hessen",                        "Hessen",
  "Rheinland-Pfalz",               "Rheinland-Pfalz und Saarland",
  "Saarland",                      "Rheinland-Pfalz und Saarland",
  "Baden-Württemberg",             "Baden-Württemberg",
  "Bayern",                        "Bayern",
  "Berlin",                        "Brandenburg und Berlin",
  "Brandenburg",                   "Brandenburg und Berlin",
  "Mecklenburg-Vorpommern",        "Mecklenburg-Vorpommern",
  "Sachsen",                       "Sachsen",
  "Sachsen-Anhalt",                "Sachsen-Anhalt",
  "Thüringen",                     "Thüringen"
)

# Dissolve the individual-state polygons into the 12 model regions.
region_sf <- bundeslaender_sf |>
  dplyr::rename(state = regional_state) |>
  dplyr::left_join(state_to_region, by = "state") |>
  dplyr::group_by(regional_state) |>
  dplyr::summarise(geometry = sf::st_union(geometry)) |>
  sf::st_as_sf()

# Predicted (fixed spline shape + region random intercept/slope, station
# effect held at population level) sowing DOY per region at the earliest
# available year (1951; the data doesn't go back to 1950) and the reference
# year (2023), avoiding extrapolation beyond the data range. The
# difference is how many days earlier sowing is "now" vs. then -- positive
# means earlier.
year_c_1951 <- min(illu$year_c)
year_c_2023 <- 2023 - 1987

pred_earlier <- expand.grid(
  year_c = c(year_c_1951, year_c_2023),
  regional_state = unique(illu$regional_state)
)
pred_earlier$predicted <- predict(model_lmm, newdata = pred_earlier, re.form = ~ (1 + year_c | regional_state))

region_earlier <- pred_earlier |>
  dplyr::mutate(when = ifelse(year_c == year_c_1951, "then", "now")) |>
  dplyr::select(regional_state, when, predicted) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = when, values_from = predicted) |>
  dplyr::mutate(days_earlier = then - now)

region_sf <- region_sf |>
  dplyr::left_join(region_earlier, by = "regional_state") |>
  # st_point_on_surface() only guarantees a point that lies inside the
  # polygon (typically the vertex of a triangulation nearest the
  # centroid) -- it isn't the region's actual center of mass. st_centroid()
  # is that area-weighted centre of gravity instead; checked separately
  # that it still lands inside all 12 (dissolved, occasionally concave)
  # regions here, so there's no need for st_point_on_surface()'s
  # inside-guarantee as a fallback.
  dplyr::mutate(label_point = sf::st_centroid(geometry)) |> 
  st_transform(crs = 25832)

# Pad the panel by 50km on every side so the map doesn't butt right up
# against Germany's own outline. region_sf is already in the metric
# EPSG:25832 CRS, so st_bbox() is in metres and can be padded directly;
# coord_sf(expand = FALSE) then uses that padded bbox as-is instead of
# adding ggplot's own (multiplicative, not a fixed distance) default
# expansion on top.
region_bbox <- sf::st_bbox(region_sf)

plot_days_earlier <- ggplot(region_sf) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(text = element_text(family = "Helvetica Neue"),
        legend.background = element_blank(),
        legend.position = c(0, 1),
        legend.justification = c(0, 1)) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = days_earlier)) +
  geom_sf_text(aes(geometry = label_point, label = sprintf("%.0f", days_earlier)), size = 4.5, family = "Helvetica Neue", colour = "grey20") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "cividis", begin = 0.5) +
  coord_sf(
    xlim = region_bbox[c("xmin", "xmax")] + c(-75000, 10000),
    ylim = region_bbox[c("ymin", "ymax")] + c(-65000, 75000),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    fill = "Estimated advance (days)\n1951–2023",
    title = "Temporal change in sugar beet sowing date",
    x = "",
    y = "",
    caption = "Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD), Climate Data Center (CDC):
                             Phenological observations of crops from sowing to harvest
                             (annual reporters, historical), Version v010, 2024.
                             
    Till Rose"
  ) +
  NULL

plot_days_earlier

```


```{r SowingDate_Trend_Diagnostics}

# Formal comparison of fixed-effect structures (all refit with ML so
# log-likelihoods/AIC are comparable; REML is only appropriate once the
# fixed-effect structure is fixed): plain linear, shared spline only,
# region-specific linear slopes as a *fixed* interaction, and the same
# regional effect as a *random* slope + intercept (model_lmm as used
# above).
model_lmm_linear_ml <- lmer(
  doy ~ Referenzjahr + (1 | Stations_id),
  data = illu,
  REML = FALSE,
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)
model_lmm_spline_ml <- lmer(
  doy ~ splines::bs(year_c, df = 5) + (1 | Stations_id),
  data = illu,
  REML = FALSE,
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)
model_lmm_region_fixed_ml <- lmer(
  doy ~ splines::bs(year_c, df = 5) + year_c:regional_state + (1 | Stations_id),
  data = illu,
  REML = FALSE,
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)
model_lmm_region_random_ml <- update(model_lmm, REML = FALSE)

AIC(model_lmm_linear_ml, model_lmm_spline_ml, model_lmm_region_fixed_ml, model_lmm_region_random_ml)

anova(model_lmm_linear_ml, model_lmm_spline_ml)
anova(model_lmm_spline_ml, model_lmm_region_fixed_ml)


aug <- broom.mixed::augment(model_lmm) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(Referenzjahr = illu$Referenzjahr)

plot_resid_fitted <- ggplot(aug, aes(x = .fitted, y = .resid)) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
  labs(x = "Fitted", y = "Residual", title = "Residuals vs fitted")

plot_resid_fitted

plot_scale_location <- ggplot(aug, aes(x = .fitted, y = sqrt(abs(.resid)))) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
  labs(x = "Fitted", y = expression(sqrt("|Residual|")), title = "Scale-location")

plot_scale_location

plot_qq_resid <- ggplot(aug, aes(sample = .resid)) +
  theme_bw() +
  stat_qq(alpha = 0.2) +
  stat_qq_line(color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Q-Q plot of residuals")

plot_qq_resid

# Normality of the station random intercepts (BLUPs)
station_ranef <- ranef(model_lmm)$Stations_id

plot_qq_ranef <- ggplot(station_ranef, aes(sample = `(Intercept)`)) +
  theme_bw() +
  stat_qq(alpha = 0.3) +
  stat_qq_line(color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Q-Q plot of station random intercepts")

plot_qq_ranef

# Residuals vs Referenzjahr: checks whether a linear trend is an adequate
# fit, or whether the true relationship is curved over time. A smooth with
# no systematic pattern around zero supports the linearity assumption.
plot_resid_year <- ggplot(aug, aes(x = Referenzjahr, y = .resid)) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
  labs(x = "Referenzjahr", y = "Residual", title = "Residuals vs Referenzjahr")

plot_resid_year


plot_resid_year_by_region <- aug |> 
  dplyr::mutate(regional_state = illu$regional_state) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = Referenzjahr, y = .resid)) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.08) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "blue", method = "loess") +
  facet_wrap(~ regional_state) +
  labs(x = "Referenzjahr", y = "Residual",
       title = "Residuals vs Referenzjahr by region (all stations pooled)")

# Pooled by region, the earlier mid-century dip / later-rise wobble mostly
# disappears -- most regions show residuals scattered flatly around zero.

plot_resid_year_by_region




top_stations <- c("7923", "8064", "8285", "8606", "10176",
                   "10619", "11174", "11220", "11725", "11803")

plot_resid_year_top_stations_pooled <- aug |> 
  dplyr::filter(Stations_id %in% top_stations) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = Referenzjahr, y = .resid)) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "blue", method = "loess") +
  labs(x = "Referenzjahr", y = "Residual",
       title = "Residuals vs Referenzjahr, 10 longest-running stations pooled (not faceted)")



plot_resid_year_top_stations_pooled
```
